text:
Situation: Propranolol hydrochloride injection has been on FDA's shortage list since 2023-10-31 and remains Current as of 2026-10-15, a duration of 36 months. Our 40 mg tablets at both Corvale sites carry NDC 71335236909 labeled by Bryant Ranch Prepack, which operates FEI 1000519407 as a registered relabel/repack plant.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspected FEI 1000519407 on 2026-07-16 and classified the inspection VAI, with the classification letter dated 2026-10-14. Earlier inspections at the same plant include an OAI classification in 2009 and multiple VAI classifications from 2010 through 2024. A Warning Letter was issued to the plant on 2010-04-08.

Our position: Corvale East holds 92 tablets (7.5 days on hand). Corvale General holds 425 tablets (29.3 days on hand). The injection shortage does not directly affect our tablet stock, but the plant's inspection history warrants monitoring.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 81 tablets of 40 mg from Corvale General to Corvale East — needs pharmacy director approval for the transfer request.
2. Evaluate AMICI PHARMACEUTICALS LLC as an alternate source — needs buyer approval; not on FDA's shortage list today and its label names no plant we could place.
3. Evaluate Advanced Rx of Tennessee, LLC as an alternate source — needs buyer approval; not on FDA's shortage list today and its label names no plant we could place.
4. Evaluate Amneal Pharmaceuticals NY LLC as an alternate source — needs buyer approval; not on FDA's shortage list today and its label names no plant we could place.
5. Evaluate AvPAK as an alternate source — needs buyer approval; not on FDA's shortage list today and its label names no plant we could place.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or therapeutic substitutions at this time; those decisions rest with treating clinicians and the committee.
